contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #262: Sharp finite-matrix Lieb–Thirring inequalities and all equality cases.
Integrated finite-matrix trace comparison and its gapless boundary extension; staged Family 262 trace assertions only.

definitions.symbol: X_s=(sI-B)^2+V for finite-dimensional complex Hermitian B,V
definitions.normalization: c_sigma>0 is the reciprocal of the integral of t^(sigma-1/2)(t^(-1/2)-(t+1)^(-1/2)) over t>0
definitions.resolvent: R(t)=pi^(-1) integral_R (X_s+tI)^(-1) ds; P(t)=t^(-1/2)I-R(t); N=c_sigma integral_0^infty t^beta P(t)dt when norm convergent
definitions.gapless_index: m is half the largest Laurent pole order of X_s^(-1) at a real singularity; m=0 if there are no singularities
definitions.positive_part: N_+ is the positive spectral part of Hermitian N

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 262 (Sharp finite-matrix Lieb–Thirring inequalities and all equality cases.; papers: Equality cases in the sharp one-dimensional matrix Lieb–Thirring inequality; Sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring inequalities for matrix potentials; Sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring constants; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/262.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
The staged trace theorems have uniform full-symbol positivity and a separate N>=0 hypothesis; trace verification alone does not certify the other manuscript dependencies.
The exact integrated trace deficit holds for all finite-dimensional Hermitian B,V with uniform symbol positivity, 0<sigma<1 and N>=0.
Coercive half-line boundary problems give Hermitian S,T, the correctly signed Riccati equations, stable spectrum, and (S+T)/2=R^-1.
The stable spectral factor evaluates the absolutely convergent logarithmic integral; its derivative is the resolvent trace difference.
The weighted integrals converge and the integration-by-parts boundary terms vanish under the stated symbol and exponent hypotheses.
Universal finite complex-matrix Riccati, inverse-trace, and ordered adjoint-square identities require no commutation of the comparison matrix with R.
The positive scalar normalization, scaling, and Tonelli identity give the exact p,q coefficients for every PSD comparison D.
For a nonnegative quadratic symbol, convergence is governed sharply by its largest inverse-symbol pole; when finite, the exact deficit extends with N_+ without assuming N>=0.
At each real singularity the inverse symbol has an even pole 2m<=2n; N converges exactly when sigma>1/2-1/(2m_max).
Nilpotent Jordan factors realize pole 2n in dimension n and hence show sharpness of the gapless convergence threshold.
An exact counterexample satisfies every hypothesis of a literal staged trace assertion.

Equality defects can be exhausted through infinitely many rows to obtain the pointwise auxiliary relations (compactness.tex).
The auxiliary relations imply fixed orthogonal channels, scalar profiles, and complex-Hermitian classification (rigidity.tex).

claims.natural_statement: Universal algebraic core for actual finite complex matrices of every dimension, with no factor-commutation assumptions: ordered factorization (sI-B+iS)(sI-B-iS)=(sI-B)^2+S^2+i(BS-SB) for every complex s; the two Riccati equations W=(L+Z)^2+i[B,L+Z]=(L-Z)^2-i[B,L-Z] imply W=L^2+Z^2+i[B,Z] and LZ+ZL+i[B,L]=0; these latter matrix relations and RL=LR=I imply tr(RW)=tr(L)-tr(RZ^2), also directly from the two Riccati equations and the inverse equations. For Hermitian U,A,H with UA=AU=I, A^2=R and U^2=L, (U-AH)^*(U-AH)=L+HRH-2H and its trace equals tr(L+RH^2-2H). For Hermitian A,Z with A^2=R, tr(RZ^2)=tr((AZ)^*(AZ)). For every finite rectangular complex X, Re tr(X^*X)>=0, hence Re tr(L+RH^2-2H)>=0 under the preceding Hermitian and inverse hypotheses. Numeric scalar 2 is nonzero over C. This claim does not assert analytic half-line existence, analytic positivity, integration, or the original full trace theorem.

import Mathlib.Data.Complex.BigOperators
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Trace
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Hermitian
import Mathlib.Tactic.NoncommRing
import Mathlib.Tactic.LinearCombination
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum

open scoped BigOperators ComplexConjugate
open Matrix

namespace TraceDeficitCore

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

theorem ordered_factorization (s : ℂ) (B S : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    (s • (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) - B + Complex.I • S) *
        (s • (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) - B - Complex.I • S) =
      (s • (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) - B) ^ 2 + S ^ 2 +
        Complex.I • (B * S - S * B) := by
  have hproduct (X : Matrix n n ℂ) :
      (X + Complex.I • S) * (X - Complex.I • S) =
        X ^ 2 + S ^ 2 + Complex.I • (S * X - X * S) := by
    noncomm_ring [smul_add, smul_sub, smul_neg, smul_smul,
      Complex.I_mul_I, neg_one_smul]
  have hcomm :
      S * (s • (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) - B) -
          (s • (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) - B) * S = B * S - S * B := by
    simp only [mul_sub, sub_mul, mul_smul_comm, smul_mul_assoc, mul_one, one_mul]
    abel
  rw [hproduct, hcomm]

theorem riccati_averaging (B L Z W : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hplus : W = (L + Z) ^ 2 + Complex.I • (B * (L + Z) - (L + Z) * B))
    (hminus : W = (L - Z) ^ 2 - Complex.I • (B * (L - Z) - (L - Z) * B)) :
    W = L ^ 2 + Z ^ 2 + Complex.I • (B * Z - Z * B) ∧
      L * Z + Z * L + Complex.I • (B * L - L * B) = 0 := by
  let P : Matrix n n ℂ := L ^ 2 + Z ^ 2 + Complex.I • (B * Z - Z * B)
  let Q : Matrix n n ℂ := L * Z + Z * L + Complex.I • (B * L - L * B)
  have hp : W = P + Q := by
    rw [hplus]
    dsimp [P, Q]
    noncomm_ring [smul_add, smul_sub, smul_neg]
  have hm : W = P - Q := by
    rw [hminus]
    dsimp [P, Q]
    noncomm_ring [smul_add, smul_sub, smul_neg]
  have hsum : Q + Q = 0 := by
    calc
      Q + Q = (P + Q) - (P - Q) := by abel
      _ = 0 := by rw [← hp, ← hm, sub_self]
  have htwo : (2 : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by norm_num
  have hQ : Q = 0 := by
    have hz : (2 : ℂ) • Q = 0 := by
      simpa only [two_smul ℂ] using hsum
    exact (smul_eq_zero.mp hz).resolve_left htwo
  exact ⟨by simpa only [hQ, add_zero] using hp, hQ⟩

theorem trace_deficit_sign (B L Z W R : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hRL : R * L = 1) (hLR : L * R = 1)
    (hW : W = L ^ 2 + Z ^ 2 + Complex.I • (B * Z - Z * B))
    (hRic : L * Z + Z * L + Complex.I • (B * L - L * B) = 0) :
    trace (R * W) = trace L - trace (R * Z ^ 2) := by
  have hcancel (X : Matrix n n ℂ) : R * (L * X) = X := by
    rw [← mul_assoc, hRL, one_mul]
  have hsand :
      Z * R + R * Z + Complex.I • (R * B - B * R) = 0 := by
    calc
      Z * R + R * Z + Complex.I • (R * B - B * R) =
          R * (L * Z + Z * L + Complex.I • (B * L - L * B)) * R := by
        simp only [mul_add, add_mul, mul_sub, sub_mul, mul_smul_comm,
          smul_mul_assoc, mul_assoc, hcancel, hLR, mul_one, smul_sub]
      _ = 0 := by rw [hRic, mul_zero, zero_mul]
  have hcycle : trace (Z * R * Z) = trace (R * Z ^ 2) := by
    rw [← trace_mul_cycle R Z Z, pow_two, mul_assoc]
  have hpower : trace (R * Z * Z) = trace (R * Z ^ 2) := by
    rw [pow_two, mul_assoc]
  have ht := congrArg (fun M : Matrix n n ℂ => trace (M * Z)) hsand
  simp only [add_mul, sub_mul, smul_mul_assoc, trace_add, trace_sub,
    trace_smul, smul_eq_mul, zero_mul, trace_zero, hcycle, hpower] at ht
  have hL : R * L ^ 2 = L := by
    rw [pow_two, hcancel L]
  have htrace :
      trace (R * W) = trace L + trace (R * Z ^ 2) +
        Complex.I * (trace (R * B * Z) - trace (B * R * Z)) := by
    rw [hW]
    simp only [mul_add, mul_sub, mul_smul_comm, trace_add, trace_sub,
      trace_smul, smul_eq_mul, hL]
    rw [← mul_assoc R B Z, ← mul_assoc R Z B, trace_mul_cycle R Z B]
  rw [htrace]
  linear_combination ht

theorem riccati_trace_deficit (B L Z W R : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hRL : R * L = 1) (hLR : L * R = 1)
    (hplus : W = (L + Z) ^ 2 + Complex.I • (B * (L + Z) - (L + Z) * B))
    (hminus : W = (L - Z) ^ 2 - Complex.I • (B * (L - Z) - (L - Z) * B)) :
    trace (R * W) = trace L - trace (R * Z ^ 2) := by
  obtain ⟨hW, hRic⟩ := riccati_averaging B L Z W hplus hminus
  exact trace_deficit_sign B L Z W R hRL hLR hW hRic

theorem ordered_adjoint_square (U A H R L : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hU : U.IsHermitian) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hH : H.IsHermitian)
    (hUA : U * A = 1) (hAU : A * U = 1)
    (hAR : A ^ 2 = R) (hUL : U ^ 2 = L) :
    (U - A * H)ᴴ * (U - A * H) =
      L + H * R * H - (2 : ℂ) • H := by
  rw [conjTranspose_sub, conjTranspose_mul, hU.eq, hA.eq, hH.eq]
  have hleft : U * (A * H) = H := by
    rw [← mul_assoc, hUA, one_mul]
  have hright : H * A * U = H := by
    rw [mul_assoc, hAU, mul_one]
  have hmiddle : (H * A) * (A * H) = H * R * H := by
    calc
      (H * A) * (A * H) = H * (A * A) * H := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = H * R * H := by rw [← pow_two, hAR]
  calc
    (U - H * A) * (U - A * H) =
        U ^ 2 - U * (A * H) - (H * A) * U + (H * A) * (A * H) := by
      noncomm_ring
    _ = L - H - H + H * R * H := by rw [hUL, hleft, hright, hmiddle]
    _ = L + H * R * H - (2 : ℂ) • H := by rw [two_smul ℂ]; abel

theorem ordered_adjoint_square_trace (U A H R L : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hU : U.IsHermitian) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hH : H.IsHermitian)
    (hUA : U * A = 1) (hAU : A * U = 1)
    (hAR : A ^ 2 = R) (hUL : U ^ 2 = L) :
    trace ((U - A * H)ᴴ * (U - A * H)) =
      trace (L + R * H ^ 2 - (2 : ℂ) • H) := by
  have hcycle : trace (H * R * H) = trace (R * H ^ 2) := by
    rw [← trace_mul_cycle R H H, pow_two, mul_assoc]
  rw [ordered_adjoint_square U A H R L hU hA hH hUA hAU hAR hUL]
  simp only [trace_sub, trace_add, hcycle]

theorem gram_trace_identity (A Z R : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hZ : Z.IsHermitian) (hAR : A ^ 2 = R) :
    trace (R * Z ^ 2) = trace ((A * Z)ᴴ * (A * Z)) := by
  have hgram : (A * Z)ᴴ * (A * Z) = Z * R * Z := by
    rw [conjTranspose_mul, hZ.eq, hA.eq]
    calc
      (Z * A) * (A * Z) = Z * (A * A) * Z := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = Z * R * Z := by rw [← pow_two, hAR]
  rw [hgram, ← trace_mul_cycle R Z Z, pow_two, mul_assoc]

omit [DecidableEq n] in
theorem gram_trace_re_nonneg {m : Type*} [Fintype m] (X : Matrix m n ℂ) :
    0 ≤ (trace (Xᴴ * X)).re := by
  classical
  simp only [Matrix.trace, Matrix.diag, Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.conjTranspose_apply,
    Complex.star_def, Complex.re_sum, ← Complex.normSq_eq_conj_mul_self, Complex.ofReal_re]
  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun j _ =>
    Finset.sum_nonneg fun k _ => Complex.normSq_nonneg (X k j)

theorem ordered_adjoint_square_trace_re_nonneg (U A H R L : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (hU : U.IsHermitian) (hA : A.IsHermitian) (hH : H.IsHermitian)
    (hUA : U * A = 1) (hAU : A * U = 1)
    (hAR : A ^ 2 = R) (hUL : U ^ 2 = L) :
    0 ≤ (trace (L + R * H ^ 2 - (2 : ℂ) • H)).re := by
  rw [← ordered_adjoint_square_trace U A H R L hU hA hH hUA hAU hAR hUL]
  exact gram_trace_re_nonneg (U - A * H)

end TraceDeficitCore

claims.natural_statement: For every n>=1, Hermitian B,V with X_s=(sI-B)^2+V>=bI for every real s and some b>0, and 0<sigma<1, N is norm convergent. If separately N>=0, continuous Hermitian L=R^-1>0,Z satisfy V+tI=L^2+Z^2+i[B,Z], LZ+ZL+i[B,L]=0, and tr(NV)-tr(N^q)=c_sigma integral t^beta (tr(RZ^2)+q||R^(-1/2)-R^(1/2)(tI+N^r)^(1/2)||_HS^2)dt.

For a nonnegative symbol X_s=(sI-B)^2+V and every t>0, the coercive half-line boundary problems give unique H^1 solutions, Hermitian S,T with V+tI=S^2+i[B,S]=T^2-i[B,T], spectrum(B+iS) in the upper half-plane, and (S+T)/2=R(t)^-1.

For every finite Hermitian B,V with X_s=(sI-B)^2+V>=0, let 2m be the largest real inverse-symbol Laurent pole, or m=0 if none. N converges in norm exactly when sigma>alpha_m, where alpha_0=0 and alpha_m=(m-1)/(2m) otherwise. Then the original exact deficit holds with N_+ in place of N in the power and square terms, without assuming N>=0, and equality holds exactly when V>=0 and [B,V]=0. The theorem includes the exact matrix resolvent asymptotic and power/log divergence constants in report equations (0)-(0a).

For a PSD Hermitian quadratic symbol X_s=(sI-B)^2+V, each real singularity has even inverse-symbol pole 2m_j<=2n with nonzero PSD leading coefficient. If m=max m_j, tr R(t) is comparable to t^(-1+1/(2m)); N is norm convergent exactly for sigma>(m-1)/(2m), with every 0<sigma<1 allowed if there is no real singularity.

For a nonnegative symbol X_s in CTX_TD with m>=1 and A_j=lim_(x->0) x^(2m_j)X_(s_j+x)^(-1), the matrix-norm limit t^(1-1/(2m))R(t) equals K=(1/m)csc(pi/(2m)) sum_(m_j=m) A_j^(1/(2m)). Put alpha_m=(m-1)/(2m). For m>1, epsilon^(alpha_m-sigma)N_epsilon tends to -c_sigma K/(alpha_m-sigma) if 0<sigma<alpha_m, and N_epsilon/log(1/epsilon) tends to -c_sigma K at sigma=alpha_m.

For every n>=1 the nilpotent Jordan factor X_s=(sI-J)^*(sI-J), with B=(J+J^*)/2 and V=J^*J-B^2, realizes inverse-symbol pole 2n with leading coefficient e_1 e_1^*. Thus sigma>(n-1)/(2n) is the sharp dimension-only convergence condition. The leading resolvent coefficient is (1/n)csc(pi/(2n))e_1 e_1^*.

The exact n=2 matrices B=[[0,1/2],[1/2,0]], V=diag(-3/16,13/16), sigma=1/2048 have noncommuting Hermitian B,V, indefinite V, X_s>=I/16 for all real s, and N>=252 c_sigma I>0; every original trace hypothesis is met.

Uniform full-symbol positivity alone does not imply N>=0: B=[[0,1/2],[1/2,0]], V=diag(-11/48,37/48), sigma=1/2 have X_s>=I/48 but N=diag((1/sqrt(3)-pi/3)/2,(1/sqrt(3)+pi/3)/2), whose first eigenvalue is negative. This is not a counterexample to the manuscript, which assumes N>=0 separately.
For B=[[0,1/2],[1/2,0]], V=diag(-1/4,3/4), sigma=1/2, the gapless symbol is PSD with inverse pole four, N=diag(-pi/4,pi/4), and tr(NV)-tr(N_+^3)=pi(16-pi^2)/64>0.
The scalar constants paper's form construction, Dirichlet approximation, spectral exhaustion, and signed-potential reduction hold (spectral.tex).
The equality paper's regularized field, primitive, positivity properties, and connecting-path foundations hold for n by d fields (appendix-paths.tex).

routes.retired_because: This scope-time plan cites superseded short claim statements. R_TD_VERIFY_EXACT records the current fully specified trace and gapless goals without changing the campaign objective.

The scoped goal and half-line statement were restated precisely and the algebra claim acquired its actual formalization. R_TD_ANALYTIC_EXACT binds the same mathematical route to all current claim versions.

The strengthened goal includes an exact leading matrix and renormalized divergence; the former three-obligation decomposition omits that new obligation. R_TD_GAPLESS_EXACT records the complete decomposition.
Commuting cases make Z=0 and the ordered comparison square vanish. Even exact commuting checks cannot establish the noncommutative theorem.
